ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within square $ABCD$, point $E$ is located on diagonal $BD$, and $BE=AB$. Connect $CE$ and $AE$. Then, what is the measure of $\angle DAE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
it follows that $\angle ABD=45^\circ$, $\angle BAD=90^\circ$,\\
since BE=AB,\\
it follows that $\angle BAE=\angle BEA= \frac{1}{2} \times (180^\circ-45^\circ)=67.5^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle DAE=\angle BAD-\angle BAE=90^\circ-67.5^\circ=\boxed{22.5^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is square ABCD, with A at the upper left corner, B at the lower left corner, C at the lower right corner, and D at the upper right corner. Diagonal BD is drawn, and point E lies on diagonal BD; line segments AE and CE are also connected, and what is asked for is the angle ∠DAE formed by AD and AE at point A. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a square, ∠DAB = 90°, and diagonal BD bisects the right angle at point B, so ∠ABD = 45°. Since E lies on BD, ∠ABE = ∠ABD = 45°. The problem gives BE = AB, so triangle ABE is an isosceles triangle, with equal base angles, that is, ∠BAE = ∠AEB. Thus ∠BAE = (180° - 45°) / 2 = 67.5°. Also because AE lies inside ∠DAB, ∠DAE = ∠DAB - ∠BAE = 90° - 67.5° = 22.5°.
